## Save Bundle (full mode only)

```{r save-bundle}
#| eval: !expr sim_mode == "full"
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Bundle assembly + saveRDS (click to expand)"

bundle <- list(
  meta = list(
    config_id         = CONFIG_ID,
    timestamp         = Sys.time(),
    n_alt             = nsims_alt,
    n_null            = nsims_null,
    sim_n             = sim_n,
    confounders       = confounders,
    fs_params         = fs_params,
    grf_params        = grf_params,
    methods_spec      = METHODS_SPEC,
    flagship_arm      = FLAGSHIP_ARM,
    diag_keep         = diag_keep,
    diag_keep_first_n = diag_keep_first_n,
    t_alt_sec         = unname(t_alt),
    t_null_sec        = unname(t_null),
    n_failed_alt      = attr(results_alt,  "n_failed"),
    n_failed_null     = attr(results_null, "n_failed"),
    package_version   = as.character(utils::packageVersion("forestsearch")),
    sessionInfo       = utils::sessionInfo()
  ),
  dgm = list(
    calibrated = dgm_calibrated,
    null       = dgm_null
  ),
  results = list(
    alt  = results_alt,
    null = results_null
  )
)

saveRDS(bundle, BUNDLE_PATH)
cat(sprintf("Bundle saved to: %s\n", BUNDLE_PATH))
cat(sprintf("  H1: %.1f min, %d rows, %d failed\n",
            t_alt  / 60, nrow(results_alt),  n_failed_alt))
cat(sprintf("  H0: %.1f min, %d rows, %d failed\n",
            t_null / 60, nrow(results_null), n_failed_null))
```

## Mode Handoff

```{r mode-handoff}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Bundle import or sim-result handoff (click to expand)"

if (sim_mode == "import") {
  bundle <- readRDS(BUNDLE_PATH)

  # Override the freshly-built DGMs with the bundle's versions so that
  # downstream OC tables match the simulation results they describe.
  dgm_calibrated <- bundle$dgm$calibrated
  dgm_null       <- bundle$dgm$null

  results_alt    <- bundle$results$alt
  results_null   <- bundle$results$null
  t_alt          <- bundle$meta$t_alt_sec
  t_null         <- bundle$meta$t_null_sec
  nsims_alt      <- bundle$meta$n_alt
  nsims_null     <- bundle$meta$n_null
  n_failed_alt   <- bundle$meta$n_failed_alt
  n_failed_null  <- bundle$meta$n_failed_null

  cat(sprintf("Imported bundle: %s\n", BUNDLE_PATH))
  cat(sprintf("  config_id : %s\n", bundle$meta$config_id))
  cat(sprintf("  timestamp : %s\n", format(bundle$meta$timestamp)))
  cat(sprintf("  n_alt     : %d (failed: %d)\n",
              nsims_alt, n_failed_alt))
  cat(sprintf("  n_null    : %d (failed: %d)\n",
              nsims_null, n_failed_null))
  if (!is.null(bundle$meta$package_version)) {
    cat(sprintf("  forestsearch %s\n", bundle$meta$package_version))
  }
  if (!is.null(bundle$meta$config_id) &&
      bundle$meta$config_id != CONFIG_ID) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "Bundle config_id ('%s') does not match this article ('%s').",
      bundle$meta$config_id, CONFIG_ID
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  cat(sprintf("Inline simulation complete (%s mode).\n", sim_mode))
}
```

# Results {#sec-results}

## Metrics Glossary {#sec-glossary}

Classification metrics follow the definitions in León et al.
(2024, Section 3).

### Detection

**Found** ($\text{any}(Q)$): proportion of simulations where
the method identifies *any* harm subgroup
($\texttt{any.H} = 1$).

- **Under H1** (alternative): $Q$ exists with a differential
  treatment effect.  $\text{any}(Q)$ is **detection power**.
- **Under H0** (null): $Q = \emptyset$ and $Q^c$ is the ITT
  population.  $\text{any}(Q)$ is the **false positive rate
  (FPR)** for falsely declaring that a harm subgroup exists.

### Classification Under H1

Under the alternative, the true harm subgroup $Q$ exists
($Q = \{\text{cd40} > 421 \cap \text{wtkg} > 82.3\}$,
prevalence $\approx$ `r sprintf("%.0f", Q_pct)`%)
with a genuinely different treatment effect (OR(Q) =
`r cal_target_or`).  Following León et al. (2024, Section 3),
define for estimated subgroup $\hat{Q}$:

$$
\text{sens}(\hat{Q}) = \frac{\#\{i \in \hat{Q} \cap Q\}}{\#\{i \in Q\}},
\quad
\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) = \frac{\#\{i \in \hat{Q} \cap Q\}}{\#\{i \in \hat{Q}\}},
$$

with analogous measures for the complement $\hat{Q}^c$.

The operating-characteristics tables report these as:

| Table column | León et al. notation | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| **Sen** | $\text{sens}(\hat{Q})$ | Fraction of true $Q$ captured by $\hat{Q}$ |
| **Spec** | $\text{sens}(\hat{Q}^c)$ | Fraction of true $Q^c$ correctly in $\hat{Q}^c$ |
| **PPV** | $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q})$ | Fraction of $\hat{Q}$ truly in $Q$ |
| **NPV** | $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}^c)$ | Fraction of $\hat{Q}^c$ truly in $Q^c$ |

Classification metrics are averaged across **all** simulations
(León et al. 2024, Table 1).  When no subgroup is detected
($\hat{Q} = \emptyset$), the simulation contributes
$\text{sens}(\hat{Q}) = 0$ and $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) = 0$
(since no member of $Q$ is captured and no subjects are
assigned to $\hat{Q}$).  This convention is implemented
at the source in `run_simulation_analysis()`, matching
the original `fs.estimates.out()` function used in
León et al. (2024).

::: {.callout-note}
## Classification metrics with discovered cuts

Because cuts are discovered from the data in this setup, a
$\hat{Q}$ that captures "roughly the right region" but with
slightly shifted boundaries will still receive high sens/PPV.
Expect these metrics to be lower than under the discretised
(oracle-cut) setup — the gap quantifies the cost of not knowing
the true cuts in advance.
:::

### Classification Under H0

Under the null, $Q = \emptyset$ --- no subgroup with a
differential treatment effect exists.  The complement $Q^c$
is the entire ITT population.  Per León et al. (2024,
Section 3), $\text{sens}(\hat{Q})$ is **undefined** (shown
as "—" in the table) and $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}) \equiv 0$.
For the complement, $\text{sens}(\hat{Q}^c) = |\hat{Q}^c|/N$
and $\text{ppv}(\hat{Q}^c) = 1$ since $Q^c$ = ITT.

The only operationally meaningful metric under H0 is the
**detection rate (FPR)**.

### Effect Estimates

All effect estimates are on the adverse scale:
OR $> 1$ = treatment (ZDV+ddI) increases the adverse outcome
(non-improvement) = **harm**.  No inversion or treatment
switching is applied.

Compare to $\widehat{|H|}$ (the FS-identified subgroup size) reported in
the row-group labels of the estimation tables below.  A ratio
$\widehat{|H|} \big/ \overline{|Q|} \approx 1$ indicates the method is

# Search-level FDR calibration {#sec-fdr-calibration}

The FS arms detect a harm subgroup under H0 at a rate of roughly 0.44 (the
`Found` column of the null operating characteristics above), even though the
thresholds (`c_screen = log(1.25)`, `c_consistency = log(1.0)`, `p* = 0.90`) were
chosen so that the *per-candidate* type-I is about 5%. The gap is multiplicity:
the search flags harm when *any* of the ~1,378 overlapping two-factor candidates
clears the rule, and that union over a correlated family is the object the
per-candidate calibration never controlled.

This section approximates that search-level rate directly with a family-level
multiplier bootstrap (companion to the resampling-theory note). For one null
trial it assembles the candidate family, re-derives each candidate's treatment
`dfbeta` through the same consistency engine the search uses, and propagates a
single multiplier vector to every candidate at once, so candidate overlap is
respected exactly; the family false-discovery probability is the fraction of
draws in which any candidate is flagged. The candidate space is rebuilt from the
analysis confounders — six continuous covariates cut at q1/median/q3 (both sides)
plus the binary factors — which reproduces the search's $L = 52$ single factors
and $1{,}378$ two-factor combinations. Two views are reported: a single
representative null trial, and an average over `r fdr_calib_nsims` null trials
that also reflects variability in how the candidate family is formed.

```{r fdr-calib-setup}
#| include: false
.fdr_files <- c("fdr_family_multiplier.R", "fdr_calibration.R")
.fdr_dir   <- getOption("fdr_src_dir", ".")
.fdr_ok    <- all(file.exists(file.path(.fdr_dir, .fdr_files)))
if (.fdr_ok) invisible(lapply(file.path(.fdr_dir, .fdr_files), source))
run_fdr_calib_eval <- isTRUE(run_fdr_calibration) && isTRUE(.fdr_ok)

# Factor family reproducing the search candidate space: continuous covariates
# cut at q1/median/q3 (both sides), binaries both levels.  unique() collapses
# tied quantiles (e.g. karnof), matching the search's redundant-cut handling.
.fdr_factors_from_conf <- function(df, cont = cont_vars, bin = bin_vars) {
  f <- list()
  for (v in cont) {
    qs   <- unique(stats::quantile(df[[v]], c(.25, .5, .75), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE))
    labs <- c("q1", "med", "q3")[seq_along(qs)]
    for (k in seq_along(qs)) {
      f[[sprintf("%s<=%s", v, labs[k])]] <- df[[v]] <= qs[k]
      f[[sprintf("%s>%s",  v, labs[k])]] <- df[[v]] >  qs[k]
    }
  }
  for (v in bin) {
    f[[sprintf("%s=1", v)]] <- df[[v]] == 1
    f[[sprintf("%s=0", v)]] <- df[[v]] == 0
  }
  f
}

# One null trial -> family-FDR threshold sweep.  beta_null is the simulated
# trial's ITT log-OR (the uniform-effect null centre); the influence matrix is
# built with the SAME adjusted logistic the search uses (y ~ treat + adjust).
.fdr_calib_one_null <- function(seed, grid) {
  df    <- simulate_from_glm_dgm(dgm_null, n = sim_n, seed = seed)
  facs  <- .fdr_factors_from_conf(df)
  cands <- enumerate_candidates(df, facs, maxk = .fs_maxk, min_n = 60L,
                                min_events_per_arm = 10L,
                                treat.name = "treat_sim", outcome.name = "y_sim")
  spec  <- list(outcome_type = "binary", effect_measure = "OR",
                treat.name = "treat_sim", outcome.name = "y_sim",
                offset.name = NULL, adjust_covariates = fs_adjust_covariates,
                adverse_outcome = TRUE)
  infl  <- build_influence_matrix(df, cands, spec)
  itt   <- as.numeric(stats::coef(glm(y_sim ~ treat_sim, family = binomial(), data = df))[["treat_sim"]])
  tab   <- calibrate_fdr_grid(infl, beta_null = itt, grid = grid,
                              draws = fdr_calib_draws, seed = seed)
  tab$n_usable  <- infl$n_usable
  tab$itt_logor <- itt
  tab
}

# Sweep: base setting (this document's thresholds) plus tighter screening / p*.
fdr_grid <- expand.grid(c_screen = log(c(fs_effect_threshold, 1.5, 1.75)),
                        p_star   = c(fs_pconsistency_threshold, 0.95, 0.975),
                        KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE)
fdr_grid$c_consistency <- log(fs_consistency_threshold)
```

```{r fdr-calib-single}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (!run_fdr_calib_eval) {
  cat(if (!isTRUE(run_fdr_calibration))
        "_FDR calibration skipped (`run_fdr_calibration = FALSE`)._\n"
      else
        paste0("_FDR calibration skipped: place `fdr_family_multiplier.R` and ",
               "`fdr_calibration.R` beside this document, or set ",
               "`options(fdr_src_dir = \"<dir>\")`._\n"))
} else {
  t1 <- .fdr_calib_one_null(fdr_calib_seed, fdr_grid)
  t1$OR_screen <- round(exp(t1$c_screen), 2)
  cat(sprintf("\n**Single null trial** (seed %d): %d usable candidates, ITT OR = %.2f.\n\n",
              fdr_calib_seed, t1$n_usable[1], exp(t1$itt_logor[1])))
  cat(knitr::kable(
        t1[order(t1$OR_screen, t1$p_star),
           c("OR_screen", "p_star", "fdr", "union_indep", "e_flagged")],
        digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
        col.names = c("OR screen", "p★", "family FDR", "indep. bound", "E[# flagged]")),
      sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}
```

The row at `OR screen = 1.25`, `p★ = 0.90` is this document's current setting; its
`family FDR` is the predicted search-level any(H) rate, to be read against the
≈0.44 observed in the null simulations above. Reading across the sweep shows
which threshold change buys the most control.

```{r fdr-calib-averaged}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (run_fdr_calib_eval) {
  seeds   <- fdr_calib_seed + seq_len(fdr_calib_nsims)
  tabs    <- lapply(seeds, .fdr_calib_one_null, grid = fdr_grid)
  fdr_mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tabs, function(t) t$fdr))   # nsims x grid rows
  agg <- data.frame(
    OR_screen = round(exp(fdr_grid$c_screen), 2),
    p_star    = fdr_grid$p_star,
    fdr_mean  = colMeans(fdr_mat),
    fdr_se    = apply(fdr_mat, 2, stats::sd) / sqrt(nrow(fdr_mat)))
  n_usable_avg <- mean(vapply(tabs, function(t) t$n_usable[1], numeric(1)))
  cat(sprintf("\n**Averaged over %d null trials** (mean usable candidates %.0f):\n\n",
              fdr_calib_nsims, n_usable_avg))
  cat(knitr::kable(
        agg[order(agg$OR_screen, agg$p_star), c("OR_screen", "p_star", "fdr_mean", "fdr_se")],
        digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
        col.names = c("OR screen", "p★", "mean family FDR", "SE")),
      sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}
```

The averaged view smooths over the trial-to-trial formation of the candidate
family. In the binary/OR null the *consistency level* `p★` is the binding lever:
raising it (a stricter one-sided confidence that the subgroup clears the harm
threshold) drives the family FDR down far faster than raising the screening OR,
because for most candidates the consistency requirement
`c_consistency + z·sigma_D` exceeds `c_screen` and is what actually binds. To
target a given search-level FDR, tighten `fs_pconsistency_threshold` first. This
diagnostic conditions on the formed candidate family and the FS/consistency arm;
the `dina-*` and `grf-*` arms use different selectors and are not covered.

#| echo: false

# Comprehensive timing summary: aggregates bootstrap, LOO, and

# left unset (e.g. when fs$sg.harm is NULL and the bootstrap was

.timing_min <- function(slot) {
  v <- timings[[slot]]
  if (is.null(v) || !is.numeric(v) || length(v) == 0L || is.na(v)) {

sim_alt_min  <- if (exists("t_alt",  inherits = FALSE) &&

# Appendix: The Pareto frontier in subgroup selection

# The dominance rule

Both objectives --- effect size and sample size --- are *maximized*. A
candidate $i$ is **dominated** if some other candidate $j$ is at least as
good on both axes and strictly better on at least one:

$$
\text{dominated}(i) \;\Longleftrightarrow\;
\exists\, j \neq i:\;
\mathrm{hr}_j \ge \mathrm{hr}_i \;\wedge\; N_j \ge N_i
\;\wedge\; (\mathrm{hr}_j > \mathrm{hr}_i \;\vee\; N_j > N_i).
$$

The **Pareto frontier** is the set of non-dominated candidates --- the
upper-right boundary of the cloud. The package implements this as an
$O(n^2)$ scan in `.pareto_dominated_xy()`; candidates with a missing
effect or size are treated as dominated. The function below is a
faithful mirror of that internal helper, kept local so this document
renders without the package; the validation section confirms the two
agree.

```{r dominance}
# Mirror of forestsearch internal .pareto_dominated_xy(): both axes maximized.
dominated_xy <- function(x, y) {
  n <- length(x)
  dom <- logical(n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (is.na(x[i]) || is.na(y[i])) { dom[i] <- TRUE; next }
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
      if (i == j) next
      if (is.na(x[j]) || is.na(y[j])) next
      if (x[j] >= x[i] && y[j] >= y[i] && (x[j] > x[i] || y[j] > y[i])) {
        dom[i] <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
  }
  dom
}
```

# How the band is formed

`.compute_inclusion_band()` builds two indicators and multiplies them:

```r
in_nbhd   <- (hr >= (1 - effect_neighborhood) * max(hr))   # 1-D effect band
in_pareto <- !dominated_xy(hr, N)                          # 2-D frontier
in_band   <- in_nbhd * in_pareto
```

Each `selection_rule` switches the two components on or off:

| `selection_rule` | `in_nbhd` | `in_pareto` | `in_band` is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"neighborhood"` | active | all ones | the effect band only |
| `"pareto"` | all ones | active | the frontier only |
| `"both"` | active | active | their intersection |

For ratio measures stored on the log scale (GLM OR/IRR), `hr` is
exponentiated before either test so the comparison is on the natural
scale; Cox HR is already natural. The neighborhood floor is a *relative*
tolerance: with `effect_neighborhood = 0.10` a candidate is in-band iff
its effect is within 10% of the strongest effect among the survivors.
Setting it to `0` collapses the band to a strict max-effect filter.

# From inclusion to selection

`sort_subgroups()` orders the candidates by a five-key lexicographic
sort and takes the top row. For `"hrMaxSG"` the key is

$$
(-\,\texttt{in\_band},\; -N,\; -\texttt{Pcons},\; -\texttt{hr},\; K),
$$

so: in-band candidates first; then the largest $N$; then higher
consistency; then higher effect; then fewer factors. `"hrMinSG"` is
identical except $N$ is minimized. Only `in_band` depends on
`selection_rule` --- the sort itself is fixed.

For the worked set, every rule that keeps `C` selects it (largest $N$ in
the band), so the **top pick is `C`** under `"neighborhood"` and
`"both"` alike; the rules differ only in whether `E` carries an in-band
flag in the diagnostic table.

## Where the rules genuinely diverge

The top selection differs only in a narrow corner: when two candidates
**tie on the maximum band $N$**, because the sort breaks $N$-ties by
consistency *before* effect, whereas Pareto dominance looks only at
(effect, $N$).

```{r corner}
corner <- data.table(
  id    = c("T", "D"),
  Pcons = c(0.95, 0.80),
  hr    = c(2.30, 2.45),
  N     = c(150L, 150L),
  K     = c(1L,   1L)
)
corner[]
```

`D` dominates `T` (equal $N$, higher HR). Under `"neighborhood"` both are
in-band, they tie on $N$, and the consistency tier keeps the
higher-`Pcons` candidate `T`. Under `"both"`, `T` is off the frontier and
excluded, so the higher-effect `D` is selected.

```{r corner-eval}
if (have_fs) {
  top_pick <- function(rule) {
    s <- forestsearch::sort_subgroups(
      data.table::copy(corner), "hrMaxSG",
      selection_rule = rule, effect_neighborhood = EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD)
    s$id[1L]
  }
  data.table(selection_rule = c("neighborhood", "both"),
             top_pick = vapply(c("neighborhood", "both"), top_pick, character(1)))
} else {
  cat("forestsearch not installed; expected: neighborhood -> T, both -> D.\n")
}
```

So `"both"` refuses to settle on a point another candidate beats on both
axes, even when it won the consistency tie; `"neighborhood"` will keep
the higher-consistency point.

# Validation against the package

Confirm the local frontier and band computations agree with the
shipped internals, and that `compute_pareto_frontier()` returns the
expected non-dominated rows.

```{r validate}
if (have_fs) {
  .ok <- function(lbl, cond)
    cat(if (isTRUE(cond)) "PASS" else "FAIL", "-", lbl, "\n")

  dt_hn <- cands[, .(hr, N)]

  pkg_dom <- forestsearch:::pareto_dominated_flags(dt_hn)
  .ok("dominated flags match .pareto_dominated_xy mirror",
      identical(pkg_dom, cands$dominated))

  pkg_nbhd <- forestsearch:::.compute_inclusion_band(
    cands$hr, cands$N, "neighborhood", EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD)
  .ok("neighborhood band matches",
      identical(as.logical(pkg_nbhd), cands$in_nbhd))

  pkg_both <- forestsearch:::.compute_inclusion_band(
    cands$hr, cands$N, "both", EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD)
  .ok("both band matches in_nbhd & on_frontier",
      identical(as.logical(pkg_both), cands$in_both))

  fr <- forestsearch:::compute_pareto_frontier(dt_hn)
  .ok("compute_pareto_frontier returns the non-dominated set",
      setequal(fr$hr, cands[on_frontier == TRUE, hr]))
} else {
  cat("forestsearch not installed; validation skipped.\n")
}
```

# Practical guidance

* `"neighborhood"` (default) asks only "is the effect close to the
  best?" then maximizes $N$. It can keep a high-consistency candidate
  that another point beats on both effect and size.
* `"pareto"` removes the `effect_neighborhood` tuning parameter
  entirely and selects on the (effect, $N$) trade-off alone --- but
  without the effect floor it will admit large-$N$, weak-effect points
  (like `F`) that the band is designed to exclude.
* `"both"` is the conservative choice: it keeps the effect floor *and*
  refuses dominated points. The in-band set under `"both"` is always a
  subset of the one under `"neighborhood"`.

The frontier here is an inclusion filter, not a stand-alone selection
criterion: the chosen subgroup still comes from the five-key sort, and
under `"hrMinSG"` the selected point may deliberately be $N$-dominated
(small subgroups are preferred). For a post-hoc *reporting* view of the
frontier independent of `sg_focus`, use `compute_pareto_frontier()` /
`pareto_frontier_table()`.

## Relationship to `dina_subgroup()`

The DINA `effMaxSG`/`effMinSG` foci reuse the same
`.compute_inclusion_band()` core, but only with
`selection_rule = "neighborhood"` --- DINA's univariate threshold
candidates form a simple effect-versus-size trade-off where the 1-D band
suffices. The `"pareto"`/`"both"` frontier variants are forestsearch-only
today; extending them to DINA would be a deliberate addition.
